title: Honor and Happiness Unite
description: Honor and Happiness Unite in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 50, “The christian”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hon-or and happ-i-ness u-nite To make the christ-ian's name a praise; How fair the scene, how clear the light, That fills the rem-nant of his days!

lines: Honor and happiness unite
To make the christian's name a praise;
How fair the scene, how clear the light,
That fills the remnant of his days!
A kingly character he bears,
No change his priestly office knows;
Unfading is the crown he wears,
His joys can never reach a close.
Adorned with glory from on high,
Salvation shines upon his face;
His robe is of th' ethereal dye,
His steps are dignity and grace.
Inferior honors he disdains,
Nor stoops to take applause from earth,
The King of kings himself, maintains
Th' expenses of his heav'nly birth.
The noblest creature seen below,
Ordained to fill a throne above;
God gives him all he can bestow,
His kingdom of eternal love!
My soul is ravished at the thought!
Methinks from earth I see him rise;
Angels congratulate his lot,
And shout him welcome to the skies!

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
